title: For statements
recap: A for loop bundles the counter initialization, condition, and increment into one header, which makes counted loops compact and keeps the loop variable scoped to the loop.
The for statement is ideal when the number of iterations is known in advance. The header clauses run in a fixed order: initialize once, then check the condition, run the body, and increment.
objectives: Implement countMultiples from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement countMultiples with a for loop. Count integers in the inclusive range [first, last] divisible by divisor. Zero counts as divisible by any positive divisor; negative multiples count too. Return 0 for first > last or divisor <= 0. Test ranges stay between -1000 and 1000, so incrementing cannot overflow.
hints: Guard against invalid divisors before using %.
The loop starts at first and includes last.
A value is divisible when value % divisor equals zero.
